# SERVSEC Crypto Project: **Secure Sessions**

This week we will secure the storage of session state across our system and on the client machine.

## 1. App: Strengthening our Web Application

- Redirect HTTP traffic to HTTPS and employ strict transport security (HSTS) for all routes

- Use WebMock to write basic tests for your Web Application’s services
  - so they do not have to connect to a real Web API.

## 2. Create a very basic (and risky!) registration workflow between App and API

- **App**: Allow users to register accounts
  - Accept posts from a registration form with email, username, and password
  - Use a service object to post the data to your API
  - _Notice_: We have not performed any verification of account details
- API: Create a Rake task (e.g., `db:bootstrap_admin`) to promote a user to admin role.

## 3. App: Encrypt session data

- Create a _secure messaging_ library that can encrypt and decrypt messages
  - Use a secret key stored in environment variable `MSG_KEY`
  - Use NaCl’s SimpleBox for all cryptography
- Create a _secure session library_ to securely set and get session variables
  - Use the secure messaging library from above for all crypto

## 4. Deploy your API and App to Heroku

- Make sure users can create/update resources on your Web app when it is deployed to the cloud

- Create Heroku dynos for your API and App
  - API: set up and integrate Postgres database
  - App: Ensure that it is talking to the deployed API

## Reference example repos

- Tyto Web API: https://github.com/ISS-Security/tyto2026-api/tree/5-deployable
- Tyto Web App: https://github.com/ISS-Security/tyto2026-app/tree/2-secure-session

## Secure Bidding System repos

- Secure Bid Web API: https://github.com/EAA-IMAGINATION/secure-bidding-api
- Secure Bid Web App: https://github.com/EAA-IMAGINATION/secure-bidding-app

## 5. App: Switch our session storage to (distributed) pool

- Use session pooling strategy on dev/test
- Use Redis as a distributed session store on production
  - Provision a Redis machine on Heroku (RedisCloud)
  - Specify Redis as our application's session store
